offence_severity: 6 months imprisonment under Section 7 and 2 years imprisonment under Section 13(1)(d) read with Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
number_of_offences: Charges under Sections 7, 13(1)(d) read with Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 were finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence of PW-8, the Under Secretary to Government, PWD, regarding the sanction order and the absence of proof of demand by the appellant.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the witnesses, noting that PW-2's testimony raised serious doubts about the acceptance of illegal gratification and the prosecution case.
bail_history: Appellant is on bail, his bail bonds stand discharged

legal_representation.accused: A Tara Chandra Sharma, Ms. Rajni K. Prasad, Ms. Nee lam Sharma, Rajeev Sharma, T. V. Ratnam, Ad vs.

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.supreme_court: Allowed appeal, set aside High Court's conviction, restored acquittal

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant demanded Rs.5,000/- as illegal gratification from PW-1 to discharge the official act of forwarding PW-1's application for pension and for release of retirement benefits. They also claimed that the sanction order was obtained and that the appellant accepted the money.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellant was on official duty in Bangalore from 07.12.1997 to 10.12.1997 and that the High Court failed to consider the alibi plea. They also contended that the High Court ignored the testimony of PW-2, who stated that the money was given for purchasing diesel, not as illegal gratification.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that 'proof of demand' is a sine qua non for constituting an offence under Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, and that mere recovery of money is not sufficient to draw the presumption under Section 20 of the Act.
precedent_relied_upon: B. Jayaraj v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2014) 13 SCC 55; P Satyanarayana Murthy v. District Inspector of Police, State of Andhra Pradesh and Anr. (2015) 10 SCC 152; Surajmal v.
